name: Kiribati
summary: A red upper half with a golden frigatebird flying over a rising sun, and a lower half of wavy blue and white bands representing the Pacific Ocean. It is based on the colonial badge of the Gilbert and Ellice Islands.
origin: The badge of the Gilbert and Ellice Islands colony, designed by Sir Arthur Grimble in 1932, showed a frigatebird over a sun and sea. At independence on 12 July 1979, Kiribati adopted a flag based on the badge's design, rejecting a version proposed by the College of Arms in favour of the local design.

symbols.name: Frigatebird
symbols.meaning: Command over the sea, freedom and power.

symbols.name: Rising sun
symbols.meaning: The 16 Gilbert Islands and Banaba (Ocean Island); also the equator, which crosses the country.

symbols.name: Wavy bands
symbols.description: Three white and three blue wavy bands.
symbols.meaning: The ocean and the three island groups: the Gilbert, Phoenix and Line Islands.

facts: Kiribati straddles both the equator and the 180th meridian.
Its Line Islands are among the first places on Earth to see each new day.
Its name is the local spelling of 'Gilberts'.
clues: A golden frigatebird over a rising sun above wavy blue and white bands.
Its sun's rays stand for 17 islands.
Its country's name is a local form of the word 'Gilberts'.
